assumptions: Impact is assumed to have begun at 22:34 UTC, when the flag began ramping and the first ZeroDivisionError appeared, rather than at 22:39 UTC when the alert fired; the alert-based window is narrower than the period customers were actually affected.

The change log returned zero deploys or releases in the 24 hours before onset; this is assumed to be complete. If an unrecorded rollout happened at 22:34, the alternative explanation (a code release introducing the faulty division) would fit the same evidence, though the successful flag revert makes it unlikely.

The specific reason the denominator is zero (e.g. an empty or zero-value spend period) was inferred from the exception type and the rendering context, not confirmed by reading the code or a stack trace.
Recovery was judged from a single observation of service metrics roughly 30 seconds after the revert; no longer soak period was observed before the incident was marked mitigated.
Only the service's own log lines and metrics were examined. Impact on downstream or dependent services, and on surfaces other than the account page, was not checked and is assumed to be none.
Who or what flipped the flag at 22:34, and whether it was an intentional rollout step, is not recorded in the evidence reviewed.
The proposed fix is a draft pull request that has not been reviewed, merged, or verified; the flag is assumed to stay off in the meantime.
input.executive_summary: Some customers loading their account page on the shop got an error instead of the page. The failures began when a new billing-related feature was switched on for live traffic at 22:34 UTC; an automated alert fired at 22:39 UTC once the failure level crossed the alerting threshold. An automated responder investigated, identified the newly enabled feature as the cause, switched it back off at 22:39 UTC, and confirmed at 22:40 UTC that the shop was serving normally again. No customer data was affected, and customers who retried after the feature was switched off would have been served normally. A draft code change to fix the underlying defect has been opened for engineering review; the feature remains off until that fix lands. Note that a low level of unrelated payment-authorization timeouts was present on the account page both before and after this incident and was not the subject of this response.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was switched on for io-shop at 22:34 (logs show it go from a steady `off` to a mixed `off 67 / on 133` ramp in that minute, then fully `on` from 22:35), which activated an account-page rendering path that performs a division with a denominator that can be zero; requests hitting that path failed with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`. No deploy or release was recorded on the service in the preceding 24 hours, and disabling the flag restored the service to baseline, so the flag enablement — not a code rollout — was the trigger for the latent bug.
